241: ✦Your baby is now aware enough to be preparing for birth.✦To leave the womb easily, they've probably turned head-down (cephalic position). If your baby hasn't turned yet this week, wait a few more weeks.✦About 96% of babies turn head-down before birth.✦In the final weeks, a head-down baby should ideally face your back (anterior position).✦This position is also an advantage for caesarean births.
242: ✦The brain and nervous system are fully developed.✦The number of brain cells keeps increasing.
243: ✦The fine hair (lanugo) on the baby's skin keeps falling out.✦The thick, white, creamy vernix caseosa that has been forming on the skin for weeks controls body temperature and protects the skin from the acidity of the amniotic fluid.✦It also helps the baby pass through the birth canal.✦In natural birth practices, the vernix is left on the skin for a while after birth – the baby isn't bathed right away.✦This way the coating keeps moisturising and nourishing the skin as the baby adapts to the outside world.✦Even if the baby is bathed within 12–24 hours, it's done so that some vernix stays on the body.
244: ✦Although the skull bones keep hardening, they're still soft.✦The skull bones haven't joined yet.✦There are soft tissues between them called fontanelles.✦These soft spots on the baby's head only close and harden fully by the time the baby is 1–1.5 years old.
245: ✦The baby's first black stool, called meconium, keeps collecting in the large intestine.✦Babies normally don't pass it before birth.✦Passing it in the womb can be a health risk.✦If this is noticed, the doctor's decisions should be followed carefully.
246: ✦Your baby has little room but still moves strongly between naps.✦You may feel hiccups too.✦If the head is down, you'll sometimes feel your baby's bottom under your ribs.✦Some mothers say they can clearly feel the pressure of their baby's feet and toes in these weeks.
247: ✦This week your baby is about 47–48 cm long, the size of a large head of lettuce.✦It weighs about 2,600–2,700 grams.
248: ✦This week you may worry, 'My baby used to kick hard, now they seem to move less.'✦But your baby's space is tight now, and they're counting the days to come out.✦There used to be room for every kind of movement in the womb.✦Now things are cramped, though there's still room to turn and wriggle.
249: ✦Once the head settles deep in the pelvis, the baby will move even less.✦So it's completely normal to feel fewer movements at 36 weeks.✦Don't expect wild somersaults and kicks like before. But if you notice anything unusual in the movements, be sure to talk to your doctor.
250: ✦You're not the only one who can't wait for your baby to arrive.✦Your little one is also aware that the journey in your belly is nearing its end.✦Your baby is preparing for birth in every way.✦Although there are about 4–6 weeks to go, they should already be in the birth position.✦Most likely the head is down and settled into the pelvis, waiting.
251: ✦The baby keeps getting longer.✦Fat keeps building up under the skin and around the organs and some muscles.✦Although surfactant production is still going on, the lungs are largely developed.✦If born this week, your baby could probably breathe without help.✦The sucking muscles will be fully developed by the end of this week, ready to breastfeed.✦The digestive system is ready too.
252: ✦The heart beats 110–150 times a minute.✦The placenta is now 20–25 cm across and 2–3 cm thick.✦This precious organ – practically everything to the baby during pregnancy – will weigh 700–750 grams at birth.
253: ✦This week black stool called meconium keeps being produced in the baby's large intestine.✦If the baby is under stress, they may pass it.✦If your waters break this week and the fluid is dark, the baby may have passed this stool in the womb.✦In that case the doctor may decide to start labour.
254: ✦This week your baby is about 48–49 cm long, the length of a long chard stalk.✦It weighs about 2,800–2,900 grams.
255: ✦Even though there are about 3 weeks left until your due week, your baby should already be in the birth position.✦Most likely the head is down and settled into the pelvis, waiting.
256: ✦The baby keeps getting longer.✦Fat keeps building up under the skin and around the organs and some muscles.✦This fat will help your baby control body temperature, grow and thrive after birth.
257: ✦At this stage the lungs are largely developed.✦If born this week, your baby could probably breathe without help.✦Finger movements and grasping have developed further.✦The baby can grasp not only their hands but also their face or toes.✦By the end of this week the sucking muscles will be fully developed, ready to breastfeed.✦The digestive system is ready for breast milk.✦The heart beats 110–150 times a minute.
258: ✦This week black stool called meconium keeps being produced in the baby's large intestine.✦If babies are under stress, they may pass it in the womb.✦If your waters break this week and the fluid is dark, the baby may have passed this stool in the womb.✦In that case the doctor may decide to start labour.
259: ✦The placenta has reached its maximum size and thickness (about 25 cm across and 2–3 cm thick).✦It will weigh 700–750 grams at birth.✦At 37 weeks, the testicles in baby boys have almost fully descended into the scrotum.
260: ✦Your baby knows your and your partner's voices very well.✦Their vision improves every week.✦This week antibodies start passing from mother to baby through the umbilical cord.✦These antibodies prepare the baby for the illnesses and germs they'll meet outside the womb.
261: ✦This week your baby is about 49–50 cm long, the size of a medium watermelon.✦It weighs about 3,000 grams.
262: ✦If your baby is born this week, they'll be fully developed, so you can relax.✦It's normal for babies to be born between 38 and 42 weeks.✦But some doctors, in many countries, wait until 41 weeks at most.✦Since the risk at 42 weeks is very low for the baby, natural-birth doctors may wait until 42 weeks in pregnancies where everything is fine.✦Waiting beyond 42 weeks isn't recommended, because the placenta's function drops a lot after that and it can be risky for the baby.✦If all is well and you want to wait, discuss this preference with your doctor in advance.
263: ✦The baby is fully mature, but brain cells keep increasing.✦So staying in the womb a little longer can still be an advantage.✦Connections are forming in the brain that will help them adapt better.✦Breathing skills and the digestive system keep getting better.
264: ✦This week the baby's heart beats 110–150 times a minute.
265: ✦Your baby's first stool, a dark green to black substance called meconium, will contain dead skin cells and lanugo.✦The lungs keep maturing and producing more surfactant (which will stop the air sacs sticking together when your baby starts breathing).✦At this stage your baby can hear your voice.✦So you and your partner should talk to them often.
266: ✦Most of the body hair has fallen out, but some babies are born with patches of lanugo that fall out in the first days or weeks.✦Since the sucking and swallowing muscles developed, your baby has been taking in amniotic fluid, and waste collects in the intestines.
267: ✦You're nearing the end of your pregnancy, and your baby keeps growing fast.✦This week is important in pregnancy.✦Your baby is now just about ready to manage on their own and adapt to the outside world.
268: ✦This week your baby is about 50–51 cm long, the size of a large pumpkin.✦It weighs about 3,300 grams.
269: ✦Your baby is mature enough to live comfortably in the outside world if born now.✦Still, brain cells keep increasing.✦Brain development in the womb is very valuable.✦In years when this wasn't known, babies born by planned caesarean were delivered at 38 weeks.✦Fortunately, unless there's a medical need, planned caesareans now require the baby to be at least 39 weeks.
270: ✦By this week most of the fine lanugo hair on the baby's body has fallen out.✦At 39 weeks, the vernix caseosa on your baby's skin keeps controlling body temperature and keeping the skin moist.✦It will also make it easier for the baby to pass through the birth canal.✦In natural birth practices, the vernix is left on the skin for a while after birth – the baby isn't bathed right away.✦This way the coating keeps the skin moist and nourished as the baby adapts to the outside world.✦At the first bath, the baby is washed so that some vernix stays on the skin.
271: ✦This week antibodies keep passing from mother to baby through the umbilical cord.✦Thanks to them, the baby will be ready for the illnesses and germs they'll meet outside the womb.
272: ✦This week fat keeps building up under the skin and around the organs and some muscles.✦Thanks to this fat, your baby's body will be able to control its temperature after birth.✦They'll need this fat for healthy growth and to thrive.
273: ✦Your baby moves less because space is tight.✦But you can still feel those tiny hands and feet pushing as they stretch.✦As the baby settles head-first into the pelvis to prepare for birth, you may feel pain and aches low down.✦In these weeks you'll feel hiccups as small rhythmic jumps.✦Since your baby moves when awake, it's good to keep track of the movements.✦If you don't feel movement for a while, be sure to talk to your doctor.
274: ✦Your baby should be in the birth position.✦Most likely the head is down and settled into the pelvis, waiting.✦In the ideal birth position, the baby faces the mother's spine.✦But the face may be turned right, left or forward.✦In such cases the baby may still move into the ideal position before birth.✦If not, the doctor may suggest turning the baby by hand.
275: ✦This week your baby is about 51–52 cm long, the size of a watermelon.✦It weighs about 3,500 grams.
276: ✦By the end of this week, the 9 months and 10 days of pregnancy will be complete.✦You may give birth this week.✦But things may not go as expected, and your baby may decide to stay a little longer.✦There's no need to worry if pregnancy goes past 40 weeks.✦According to medical guidelines, as long as everything is fine, the baby can be awaited until 42 weeks.✦In that case your doctor will suggest monitoring the baby more often.✦Some doctors wait until 41 weeks.✦How long doctors wait differs between hospitals and countries.✦Waiting times also vary between individual doctors.✦Many doctors who don't wait until 42 weeks prefer not to take on the legal risk.✦Doctors who do wait until 42 weeks trust the nature of mother and baby, are experienced in normal birth, and know there's no medical problem in waiting as long as all is well.
277: ✦When your baby is born, the nurse clears mucus and amniotic fluid from the baby's mouth and nose.✦Surfactant, produced since the last trimester, does its job right after birth by helping the lungs inflate.✦This lets the baby breathe easily on arrival.✦Because premature babies haven't finished producing surfactant, they're given artificial surfactant and breathing support in an incubator.
278: ✦When your baby comes out, you may see them still curled up in the fetal position.✦That's simply out of habit and comfort.✦After 9 months in a tight womb, it can take time for them to realise there's room to stretch out.
279: ✦If you're not showing signs of labour yet, don't be disappointed.✦About 50% of pregnancies last longer than 40 weeks.✦Many doctors normally allow pregnancy to continue until 42 weeks.✦If labour doesn't start on its own, your doctor will induce it at 41 or 42 weeks.
280: ✦Your baby is in your arms at last! You've reached the end of a 9-month marathon.✦And the lovely days ahead aren't limited to this excitement – first teeth, first milestones and the first birthday will keep adding new joys every day.✦'Look, they're crawling!', 'Look, a tooth!', 'They said mama/dada!' – the excitement never ends! 🙂
